subject: chemistry

moments.title: Nicholson and Carlisle electrolyse water
moments.body: Days after Volta's pile is described in print, Nicholson and Carlisle use one to electrolyse water into H2 and O2. The first electrochemical decomposition.
moments.takeaway: Within weeks of the first battery, water is split into its elements.

moments.title: Faraday's laws
moments.body: Faraday formulates his two laws of electrolysis: mass deposited is proportional to charge, and to equivalent weight. Electrochemistry becomes quantitative.

moments.title: Hall-Héroult aluminium
moments.body: Simultaneously and independently, two 22-year-olds develop the electrolytic process for aluminium. Aluminium goes from precious metal (Napoleon's banquet plates) to cheap commodity within a decade.
moments.takeaway: Aluminium becomes a mass commodity through electrolysis.

moments.title: Green hydrogen
moments.body: Electrolysers powered by renewable electricity produce green H2 for steel, ammonia, transport. Scale-up to GW-class plants is happening in 2024-2030.
moments.takeaway: Electrolysis may yet decarbonise heavy industry.

now.title: Where we are today
now.body: Electrolysis is being scaled massively for green H2. PEM and alkaline electrolysers compete; solid-oxide and AEM emerging. Catalysis improvements reduce iridium and platinum use.
now.open_questions: Can green H2 be produced at cost-competitive levels by 2030?

reflection: Hall and Héroult independently solved aluminium electrolysis in the same year. How often does technology emerge when its time comes?
